analyst_view.overall: This is a top-four clash: Ajax are second and Twente fourth. Both won in the Conference League on Thursday, Twente 3-1 against Pafos and Ajax 6-1 at Midtjylland. John van den Brom has a fit squad apart from Unnerstall, Lemkin, Bruns and Thorvaldsen, and he expects Ajax to attack far more than Pafos did. For Ajax, Míchel says Caio Henrique and Oliver Edvardsen are available, Julian Brandt is ready, and Sofyan Amrabat may be fit, so Ajax are stronger than the site's injury list suggests.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals. Both attacks are in form, with Twente scoring 20 in their last six and Ajax 17. Van den Brom expects both sides to go for the win, and Ajax's returning players, including Brandt and Edvardsen, strengthen the visitors' attack.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.9 corners, most of them expected for Twente. An Ajax side that attacks more should win more corners than the model's share, but Twente may win fewer, so the total stays around the model.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.1 cards, with Joey Kooij refereeing, and he shows slightly more cards than average. It is a big game, but both teams have been booked less than expected recently, and we found no disciplinary news. We stay with the model.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.8 shots, with Twente expected to take nearly twice as many as Ajax. Van den Brom expects Ajax to come forward, which should balance the split more than the model does. The total already allows for a busy game, so we stay close to it.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.6 shots on target. Both teams have put more shots on target than expected in their last six, and Ajax's attack gets Brandt back behind Tolu Arokodare. We expect a few more efforts on target than the model.
